summary: Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has taught at the University of Hong Kong and held a post at Renmin University of China from approximately 2006 to 2020.
Weiru Guan specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where she studied under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).
Wen-ling Jane focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University, where she studied with doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, and Peking University (PhD), and served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. After completing a PhD at Stanford University in 1998, she held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018).

Wendy Doniger is an Indologist and historian of religions. Educated at Radcliffe College, Harvard University (MA, PhD), and Oxford (DPhil), she served at the University of Chicago from 1978 to 2018 as Mircea Eliade Distinguished Service Professor.

Wenjiang Ding was a Chinese scholar active in history and archaeology. He studied under Liang Qichao (~1902–1904) and at Peking University, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1931 to 1934.

Wenjie Duan was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts, he held multiple leadership posts at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946 to 1998.

Wenjie Qin specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Tu Weiming, studying with Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

Werner Abraham was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the University of Tübingen, and a full professorship at the University of Groningen starting in 1971.

Werner Sundermann was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Berlin (~1958–1967), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1967–1991), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
Wes Borton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Derek F. Maher at East Carolina University and later studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1968–1975) and served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1974–1977) and the University of California, Davis (~1977).

Whitney Cox specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago (~2000–2006) under Sheldon Pollock, later holding an academic post at SOAS University of London (~2006–2013).

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ceylon and SOAS, later serving at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973), University of Peradeniya (1964), and University of Kelaniya (~1956–1986).

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He completed master's studies at the University of Colorado and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton. He held major posts at Forman Christian College (1940–1946), McGill University (1948–1951), Harvard University (1964–1985), Dalhousie University (1974), and Trinity College, Toronto (1985).

Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and held a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

Wilhelm Deecke was a linguist who earned his doctorate at Leipzig (1848–1849) and studied in Berlin under Bopp and Weber. He served as a school director and leader at Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Jean Sturm, Gymnasium Buchsweiler, and Lycée de Mulhouse.

Wilhelm Dilthey was a philosopher educated at Heidelberg and Berlin. He held academic positions at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel University (~1868–1871), University of Breslau (~1871–1882), and the University of Berlin (~1882–1905).
